questions.question: A previously healthy man aged approximately 45 years presents after three weeks of progressively worsening non‑tender cervical edema involving the strap muscles demonstrated on CT scan. He reports mild proximal hip flexor weakness (strength 4/5), has a modestly elevated CRP (~55 mg/L), a normal white blood cell count, is afebrile and denies recent ACE‑inhibitor use or other medication exposure known to precipitate angioedema. Complement studies (C3/C4/C1‑esterase inhibitor activity) are normal. Which single initial laboratory test would best help distinguish an infectious deep‑neck space process from an inflammatory myopathy?

A patient presents with cervical soft tissue swelling that clinically resembles angioedema but does not respond to antihistamines or C1‑esterase inhibitor replacement therapy; C4 levels are normal while serum creatine kinase is markedly elevated together with proximal muscle weakness. List three bedside clinical or laboratory findings that favor pseudo‑angioedema due to dermatomyositis over classic histamine‑mediated or bradykinin‑mediated angioedema.

Anti–small ubiquitin-like modifier activating enzyme subunit 1 (anti‑SAE1) antibodies are strongly associated with a subset of dermatomyositis patients. Describe how these antibodies interfere with the SUMOylation pathway and how this disruption contributes mechanistically to the characteristic perifascicular microvascular injury seen in skin and muscle biopsies.

During your bedside examination you note periungual erythema with capillary loop hemorrhages, subtle facial erythema over the nasolabial folds (“holster sign”), and a faint erythematous rash over the lateral thigh while assessing a patient whose chief complaint is cervical swelling. How do these cutaneous findings assist in recognizing an underlying inflammatory myopathy such as dermatomyositus before serologic confirmation?

"High dose" intravenous methylprednisolone followed by oral prednisone taper was coupled with intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), mycophenolate mofetil, and rituximab in this patient, while methotrexate was deliberately avoided because of emerging interstitial lung changes. Explain the rationale for selecting this particular combination regimen over conventional methotrexate‑based steroid sparing therapy.

"Trimethoprim–sulfamethoxazole" was initiated for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia prophylaxis but had to be stopped after the patient developed hemolytic anemia despite a negative G6PD screen. What alternative prophylactic regimens can be employed for PCP prevention in patients receiving high‑dose glucocorticoids together with additional immunosuppressants who cannot tolerate TMP–SMX?

"Serial creatine kinase" trends are frequently used to monitor therapeutic response in inflammatory myopathies. Beyond CK levels alone, name two additional clinical or laboratory parameters that should be followed longitudinally in patients treated for dermatomyositis receiving immunosuppression and explain why they are important.
